page: Google Cloud Platform c4d-standard-64-lssd is a general-purpose virtual machine equipped with 64 vCPUs and 248 GB of memory, maintaining a balanced ratio of roughly 3.88 GB of RAM per vCPU. The instance is powered by dedicated AMD EPYC 9B45 processors on the x86_64 architecture, presenting 32 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading. It includes advanced instruction support such as AVX-512, AVX-VNNI, and cryptographic acceleration via VAES and SHA-NI. The server bundles 2,412 GB of high-speed local NVMe solid-state storage across six drives, providing direct high-throughput disk access without relying solely on network-attached storage.

Benchmark evaluations position this instance in the top 10 percent for single-core and multi-core computational tasks, reflected by a Geekbench multi-core score of 26,866 and a PassMark CPU score of 92,193.75. Memory performance remains competitive, registering an uncached read bandwidth of 206.38 GB/sec and a write bandwidth of 136.56 GB/sec. Application benchmarks show high transaction capabilities, executing over 113.85 million Redis SET operations per second and scoring in the top tier for database operations and software compilation.

The inclusion of large local NVMe storage combined with strong per-core compute makes the c4d-standard-64-lssd cost-efficient for heavy data-processing environments where attached storage latency would present a bottleneck. The primary architectural tradeoff is the ephemeral nature of local SSD storage, which requires application-level replication strategies to safeguard data. The server is well matched for transactional databases, in-memory caching systems, CI/CD compilation pipelines, and container host environments requiring rapid local read and write operations.
description: Google Cloud Platform c4d-standard-64-lssd is a general-purpose compute instance featuring 64 vCPUs across 32 physical cores of an AMD EPYC 9B45 processor and 248 GB of system memory. Built on the x86_64 architecture with AVX-512 and cryptographic extensions, the instance includes 2,412 GB of integrated local NVMe SSD storage. Benchmark metrics show top-tier execution across single-core and multi-core evaluations, including high ratings in Geekbench, software compilation, and PassMark database operations, along with Redis throughput exceeding 113 million operations per second. Lacking hardware GPU acceleration and persistent local disk retention, the configuration trades off permanent onboard storage for direct NVMe IOPS and low latency. This profile delivers high operational density for transactional databases, CI/CD build clusters, distributed caching, and data-intensive enterprise backends.
